Evidence: Source 1 and Source 3 confirm that during the Palghar Lok Sabha by-election campaign in May 2018, Uddhav Thackeray addressed rallies in Vasai and Mokhada. In these speeches, Thackeray made several allegations against the BJP. He claimed the BJP lacked ideals and that individuals could join the party if they showed 'money bags' (Source 3). He also accused the BJP of not wanting opposition to projects like the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train and the Mumbai-Nashik expressway (Source 1). Furthermore, Thackeray criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for spending excessive time abroad and accused the BJP of mistreating the family of the late MP Chintaman Wanaga (Source 1, Source 3). He warned that the Shiv Sena would use 'danda' (muscle power) if the BJP cracked down on those opposing government projects.
Justification: The retrieved evidence confirms that Uddhav Thackeray made significant allegations against the BJP during the Palghar by-election campaign. Source 3 explicitly states that Thackeray attacked the BJP by claiming it had no ideals left and that entry into the party was based on 'money bags'. Additionally, Source 1 details Thackeray's accusations regarding the BJP's stance on infrastructure projects and his criticism of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. These statements directly corroborate the claim that Thackeray made major allegations against the BJP during the Palghar by-election. The evidence clearly establishes that Thackeray used his campaign platform to level these specific charges against the party and its leadership, thereby supporting the claim's core assertion.
